title: Atlas discovery observation batch (v1)
description: The public wire format a discovery scanner emits INTO Atlas: a batch of raw observations of an IT landscape (servers, applications, infrastructure, and the data layer down to data-areas, datasets and columns) that the private Atlas Enterprise reconciliation engine correlates, deduplicates and turns into catalogue assets. This contract carries facts only — an observation has no Atlas 'id' and no 'lifecycle' (the reconciler assigns those), and never any analysis (no EOL/risk, no criticality, no portfolio scoring). Open so third parties can build scanners; the reconciliation logic that consumes it is the private moat and is NOT part of this repo. See handbook 11 §3, 12 §Phase A, and vev-software/atlas-enterprise#6/#9.

contractVersion.description: The atlas-contracts schema major version this batch conforms to.

kind.description: Discriminates a discovery observation batch from the import/export documents.

source.description: Provenance of the batch: which scanner produced it and how.

observedAt.description: When the scan that produced this batch was taken.

observations.description: The raw observations in this batch. May be empty (a scan that saw nothing new).

ObservationSource.description: Which scanner produced the batch. The authoritative tenant binding is the authenticated machine-principal at ingestion (a Fabric concern), NOT this payload; 'tenantRef' is an optional, opaque hint only.

agentId.description: Stable identifier of the emitting agent or collector. Constant across scans so the reconciler can attribute observations to a source.

method.description: How the batch was collected: an installed 'agent' in the landscape, or 'agentless' remote scanning from a collector.

tenantRef.description: Optional opaque tenant hint. Not authoritative — ingestion binds tenancy from the authenticated principal.

Observation.description: A single raw sighting of something in the landscape. Facts only: no Atlas 'id' and no 'lifecycle' (the private reconciler assigns identity and catalogue state), and no analysis. Kind-specific held facts reuse the catalogue vocabulary; discovery-only facts (ports/processes/packages) are additional observations, not catalogue analysis.

observedId.description: A scanner-local identifier for the observed thing, stable across scans from the same source. NOT an Atlas asset id — the reconciler decides the catalogue identity.

fingerprint.description: Durable attributes the reconciler may correlate on (e.g. machine-id, MAC, serial, cloud instance id) — deliberately more than a hostname. Carried as facts; how they are weighted for matching is private reconciler logic, not part of this contract.

ports.description: Observed listening ports (a fact, not an integration map).

tags.description: Observed lightweight labels (e.g. a cloud resource tag).

firstSeen.description: When the source first saw this thing, if tracked.

lastSeen.description: When the source most recently saw this thing, if tracked.

FingerprintAttribute.description: One durable correlation attribute: a key and its observed value (both required — unlike a Tag, a fingerprint carries no valueless keys).

ObservedPort.description: An observed listening port. A recorded fact; not a measured integration.

address.description: The bind address the port was seen on, if known.

ObservedProcess.description: An observed running process or service. A recorded fact.

port.description: The port the process was seen listening on, if known.

ObservedPackage.description: An observed installed runtime or package. A recorded fact; the version is what was seen, not an EOL/risk assessment (that is paid Atlas core).
